logline: A retired Punjab police officer's family makes one catastrophic decision to protect their son, and Tabbar watches the moral scaffolding collapse across eight relentless episodes of domestic noir.

bollymeter.basis: Won 8 Filmfare OTT Awards including Best Series (Critics) and Best Actor (Malhotra) - a clean sweep that reflected a genuine critical consensus. IMDb audience settled at 8.3. Director Ajitpal Singh and writer Harman Wadala were both cited as breakout names in Indian OTT writing and direction.

pull_quotes.text: Pavan Malhotra-led thriller is as dark as it gets - without a minute of ease.

seasons.review_body: Tabbar is built around a Punjabi middle-class family whose defining feature - the ferocious instinct to protect their own - is exactly what destroys them. Pavan Malhotra's Omkar Singh is a retired police sub-inspector who has spent his career knowing exactly how crime works, which makes his choices more damning, not less. Supriya Pathak's Sargun is arguably the show's moral centre and its most complex character - a woman who absorbs every consequence with total deliberateness. Gagan Arora, as the son who sets everything in motion, is terrifyingly good at making sympathy and revulsion coexist. Director Ajitpal Singh, who made Of Fathers and Sons, brings a documentary restraint to the thriller mechanics - there are no stylistic pyrotechnics, just the slow constriction of a trap being built one domestic detail at a time. The show doesn't judge its characters; it simply watches them. That refusal to editorialize is what distinguishes it from the dozens of Indian crime dramas that deploy moral chaos as entertainment.

episode_reviews.title: Ik Jhooth
episode_reviews.review_body: Tabbar Season 1 Episode 1 'Ik Jhooth' aired October 15, 2021 on SonyLIV as the premiere of the eight-episode series. The show won 8 Filmfare OTT Awards including Best Series (Critics) and Best Actor for Pavan Malhotra; IMDb audience scored it 8.3. High on Films praised a 'first episode that trusts silence where lesser shows would reach for music.' The premiere establishes the Singh family in their comfortable Punjab domesticity before one night fractures everything. Director Ajitpal Singh's pacing is deliberately unhurried: this is a family the audience understands before it makes a choice that cannot be taken back. Pavan Malhotra's Omkar has spent decades on the right side of the law, and the premiere communicates precisely what that means when the law becomes the thing he must now evade. The episode's final scene is among the most quietly devastating in recent Indian streaming.

episode_reviews.the_moment: Omkar's face in the moment he decides to protect his son - the precise second a good man chooses to become something else.

episode_reviews.title: Aadha Sach
episode_reviews.review_body: Tabbar Season 1 Episode 5 'Aadha Sach' aired October 15, 2021 on SonyLIV. The show won 8 Filmfare OTT Awards including Best Actor for Pavan Malhotra; IMDb audience scored it 8.3. Koimoi called the series 'as dark as it gets - without a minute of ease.' The midpoint episode is where the Singh family's cover story begins fracturing simultaneously from multiple directions. Ranvir Shorey's antagonist closes in; Sargun's resourcefulness is tested to its limit. The writing is at its tightest here - each scene adds pressure without the show needing to raise its voice. Supriya Pathak's Sargun, described by Nirvaan Diaries as the show's secret engine, has her most demanding material in this episode: a woman absorbing every consequence with total deliberateness, in a kitchen conversation at 2am with her husband that treats the unthinkable as a domestic problem requiring a domestic solution.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The midpoint episode where the Singh family's cover story begins to fracture simultaneously from multiple directions. Ranvir Shorey's antagonist closes in; Sargun's resourcefulness is tested to its limit. The writing here is at its tightest - each scene tightens the coil without the show needing to raise its voice.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Sargun and Omkar's conversation in the kitchen at 2am - the domestic register of a marriage dealing with the unthinkable.

critic_note.text: Supriya Pathak is the show's secret engine - and episode five is where the engine runs hottest.
